learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover how we acquire new behaviors, habits, skills, and knowledge through experience, association, and consequences!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Learning is any relatively permanent change in behavior or behavioral potential produced by experience. (Note: changes due to fatigue, drugs, or maturation are not learning).

Discovered by Ivan Pavlov. It's learning by association. A neutral stimulus (a bell) is paired with a natural stimulus (food) until the neutral stimulus alone causes the natural response (salivation).
Developed by B.F. Skinner. Learning is based on consequences. Behaviors followed by rewards (reinforcement) are more likely to be repeated, while those followed by punishment are less likely.
Albert Bandura showed that we learn by watching others (models) and imitating them, even without direct rewards. (e.g., children imitating aggression from a video).
Learning that involves mental processes, thinking, and knowing. Examples include insight learning (the sudden 'Aha!' moment) and latent learning (learning that occurs but is not immediately shown).

fun_activity.title: 🐶 The Animal Trainer
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a bad habit you want to break or a good habit you want to build (like making your bed). Design a quick 'Operant Conditioning' system for yourself. What will be your positive reinforcement (reward) when you do it?

exam_tips: 📌 Always use Pavlov's dog experiment to explain Classical Conditioning.
📌 Distinguish between Negative Reinforcement (removing a bad thing to increase behavior) and Punishment (adding a bad thing to decrease behavior).
📌 Extinction happens when the conditioned response gradually fades away because the reward/unconditioned stimulus is stopped.
quick_recap: ⭐ Unconditioned Stimulus (US) naturally triggers a response without learning.
⭐ Shaping is the process of rewarding successive approximations of a desired behavior.
⭐ Transfer of learning occurs when past learning affects the learning of a new skill (can be positive, negative, or zero).
